newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-NEWCASTLE WIN BRINGS CHAMPIONS LEAGUE INTO FOCUS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NEWCASTLE WIN BRINGS CHAMPIONS LEAGUE INTO FOCUS.

text.p: Newcastle's 1-0 win over Arsenal at Highbury on Saturday finally killed off the Gunners' faint title hopes and at the same time kept alive United's hopes of a place in the European Champions' League next season.
Newcastle remained fourth in the table but, with three games left, improved their chances of finishing second to likely champions Manchester United.

That would give them England's second spot in the expanded Champions' League -- and until Monday at least, Newcastle also have a mathematical chance of winning the title outright, something they have not done since 1927.

That slim chance will disappear if Manchester United beat relegation-threatened Middlesbrough at Old Trafford on Monday afternoon. But if Manchester United were to lose their last three games and Newcastle won their last three -- including a win over Manchester United at Old Trafford next Thursday -- Newcastle could yet be chamnpions.

Manager Kenny Dalglish knows that is only an extremely faint possibility but said after his team's victory: "At least we've made sure we are in Europe again next season and that is some reward for our consistency in the league lately.
"Winning today made sure of a place in the UEFA Cup at least and maybe we can go on and get a bit more out of the season yet.
"The three points were probably flattering to us today but you can always look back at other games where you thought you deserved something and didn't get it."
Dalglish admitted his team were flattered by the win which was sealed when Robbie Elliott headed home deep into injury time at the end of the first half.

Their cause was made no easier against an Arsenal side who had 20 goal attempts when substitute Keith Gillespie was sent off 11 minutes from time for a second bookable offence. He kicked the ball away in a temper for his first yellow card, then tripped Nigel Winterburn to earn a red one.
But Newcastle won because transfer-listed Czech goalkeeper Pavel Srnicek had an outstanding match and because the back line held firm despite some intense Arsenal pressure.

Srnicek, who had not played in the first team since December 26, was a late replacement for Shaka Hislop who felt ill before the match. He made several outstanding saves, especially from Ian Wright and Dennis Bergkamp.

Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, who initially counted his team out of the title race two months ago but then saw them come right back into contention with only one defeat in their last eight games, conceded afterwards: "I don't think we can finish second now and it is very frustrating. It's a big disappointment.
"We were unlucky today but added to the other big home defeats we have had against Manchester United and Liverpool it shows that losing at home is not a coincidence.
"Newcastle did the minimum today but we were not creative enough or penetrative enough and it shows we have a problem playing at home."

Perhaps because the chance of finishing second and reaching the Champions' League was at stake, the match was an untidy, scappy one, with referee Martin Bodenham booking 10 players as well as sending off Gillespie.
Asked what his impression of the match was, Dalglish, famous for his dead-pan one liners, replied: "The best you could say is that it was interrupted by a lot of cautions."
The only goal came when Elliott headed home after Arsenal failed to clear a corner.
England goalkeeper David Seaman had just made an excellent save to turn a Lee Clark shot round the post but Arsenal failed to clear the corner that followed.
Darren Peacock won possession to hook the ball back into the goalmouth, where Elliott ran in to nod home.
